chunks: 3117 - Abu Abdullah عليه السلام and Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام said:

Whoever forgets the sa'i until he has proceeded through part of it or all of it, then remembers, should not turn his face away departing; rather, he should return backward to the place from which the sa'i is required.

key_terms.السَّعْيِ: the ritual walking between al-Safa and al-Marwah in hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.الْقَهْقَرَى: walking backward or returning in reverse
key_terms.الْمَكَانِ: the place to which one must return

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he forgets part of the sa'i and then remembers?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who forgets part or all of the sa'i during hajj or 'umrah. Upon remembering, the person should not turn around in the usual manner, but should return backward to the point from which the sa'i must be resumed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3117 - Abu Abdullah (as) and Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) said:

"Whoever forgets a part or all of the Sa’i (ritual walking) and remembers it, should not turn around and walk away from the direction of Sa’i. Instead, he should go back in reverse to the place where the Sa’i is required to be resumed."
